function: Joint channel estimation, detection and LDPC decoding receiver recovering the information bits from pilots and received signals, using unfolded ADMM networks JCDDNet-G and JCDDNet-S (pp. 1, 3).
system: Coded single-carrier MIMO with Nt=4, Nr=8 (Gaussian); mmWave with 2x2 UPA transmitter and 8x8 UPA receiver; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Deep unfolding of relaxed and accelerated ADMM with layer-wise trainable penalty, relaxation, and predictor parameters; supervised offline training on transmitted-bit labels (Adam, multi-stage, 10000 samples) (pp. 6, 8, 10).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. and Kronecker-correlated Gaussian MIMO channels (Nr=8, Nt=4); Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel (8 clusters, 10 paths); LDPC code N=288 plus CCSDS codes (pp. 9, 13).
test_conditions: Training: 10000 samples at one SNR with ADMM BLER 1e-2; testing: other SNRs and new channel realizations, plus unseen correlation 0.3 and codelength 144 (pp. 10, 13).
baselines: Decoupled, IDD, and ICDD turbo receivers with MMSE, GAMP, or MAP detectors; LMMSE or ISTA channel estimation; ICDD with virtual-pilot selection [17]; untrained ADMM (JCDD-G) (pp. 9-11).
metrics: BLER versus SNR; average iterations/layers and CPU time per codeword; number of real-valued operations (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Table I lists real-valued operation counts per codeword; JCDDNet needs about 1.1e5 operations per layer, near-linear in codelength; Table II gives CPU time (p. 14).
openness: Source code at https://github.com/sunyi0101/JCDDNet (p. 10, footnote 3); data are simulated.
q1_support: p. 9: "the Saleh-Valenzuela model is" used for the mmWave channel, and i.i.d. and Kronecker-correlated Gaussian channels for the other receiver. Not met: custom simulators with textbook models; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "directly applying the parameters trained" under i.i.d. Gaussian channels, tested on correlated channels with rho = 0.3 (Fig. 10); "evaluated with C2 of codelength" N = 144 after training with C1 of N = 288 (Fig. 11).
q3_support: p. 9: "The traditional decoupled and turbo receivers, including" the IDD and ICDD (MMSE, GAMP, MAP detectors) are the baselines, all non-learned. Not met: no earlier learned receiver such as DeepRx or the autoencoder, cited only in the introduction (p. 2), is compared; the untrained ADMM JCDD-G is a variant of the proposed method (p. 11).
q4_support: p. 14: "require only 1.1e5 operations per layer"; Table I gives the real-valued operation counts of all receivers per codeword and Table II the average CPU time (p. 14).
notes: Area 1 over area 2: the method solves channel estimation, detection and decoding jointly, and its main metric is the BLER of the recovered bits (Figs. 5-12) with no channel-estimation error reported; p. 3: "The ultimate goal of the receiver is to recover the information bits". Deep unfolding with trained parameters counts as learned. Generalization is shown only for mild mismatch; p. 13 admits failure for strongly deviating channel distributions or codes. The PDF is arXiv 2404.07721v1 (11 Apr 2024), titled Trainable Joint Channel Estimation, Detection and Decoding for MIMO URLLC Systems.
